---
title: "Pipeline and codec"
bibliography: ../references.bib
---

`compress_bin_to_h5` turns a raw 2500 Hz SpikeGLX LFP binary into an lfpack file in two
stages: preprocessing to a denoised 250 Hz float32 array (checkpointed as `.npy`), then the
codec. `compress_to_h5` runs the codec alone.

## Preprocessing

| Step | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Saturation | ADC-clipped spans detected on the raw band (amplitude only), stored as an interval table | Found before filtering smears them; muted at the end |
| Bad channels | `ibldsp.voltage.detect_bad_channels_cbin` [@ibl2022spike]: good, dead, noisy, outside the brain; stored as `labels` | Incoherent channels inflate the SVD noise floor |
| Dephasing | NP1 per-channel sub-sample shift (`ibldsp.fourier.fshift`) | Aligns the channels' sampling times |
| Highpass | 0.5 Hz zero-phase Butterworth, recording ends apodised | Removes drift, keeps delta and infra-slow activity |
| Interpolation | Bad channels replaced from their neighbours | |
| CAR | Median across channels subtracted | Common-mode noise |
| Decimation | 2500 → 250 Hz FIR (`q=10`) | The LFP band sits well below 125 Hz |
| Cadzow | F-X Cadzow denoising, when `cadzow_kwargs` is given | Removes incoherent channel noise before the SVD |
| Muting | Saturated spans zeroed with a short cosine taper, after Cadzow | Muting earlier leaks energy back through the filters |

F-X Cadzow works frequency bin by frequency bin (up to `fmax`): the complex channel vector
of each spatial window is laid out as a block-Toeplitz matrix over the probe geometry,
truncated to a low rank, and averaged back to channels. IBL runs it with
`dict(rank=5, niter=1, fmax=None, nswx=64, ovx=32, gap_threshold=2.0, ppca_k=2.0)`.

## Codec {#codec}

The 250 Hz array is cut into 8 s chunks $X_j$ (2048 samples, coded with 128 guard samples on
each side so wavelet edge effects fall outside the written samples).

**Spatial stage.** Each chunk is factorised $X_j \approx U_j\,\mathrm{diag}(s_j)\,V_j^\top$
with rank $r_j = \#\{k : s_k > \varepsilon\,\sigma_0\}$, where $\sigma_0$ is the median of the
lower half of the singular values. At ε = 100 the rank is about 17. The spatial modes of a
recording barely move over a session, so the file stores one basis $B$ (nc × 32) per
recording and, per chunk, float16 coefficients $C_j$ with $U_j s_j \approx B\,C_j$. This costs
< 0.01 dB of SNR and shrinks the spatial part about 20×.

**Temporal stage.** Each row of $V_j^\top$ is decomposed into db4 level-5 wavelet packets and
hard-thresholded at $\tau_k = \alpha\,\sigma_0 / s_k$. Every discarded coefficient therefore
costs less than $\alpha\,\sigma_0$ of reconstruction error, whatever the mode, and strong
modes keep more temporal detail than weak ones. The dominant row always keeps its
`floor_k = 64` largest coefficients so a low-SNR chunk never decodes to zero; a muted chunk
still decodes to exactly zero.

## Choosing ε and α

Measured on 11 IBL NP1 recordings, with behaviour decoding (wheel speed from LFP band power)
run on every reconstruction:

![File size vs change in wheel-speed R² (top) and SNR (bottom) against the former 0.4 "mild" tier (ε = 100, α = 14, per-chunk U), mean ± s.e.m. over 11 recordings. Left: rank threshold ε; right: basis size and coefficient precision. Dotted: uncompressed data.](../figures/codec_pareto.png){.lightbox}

- **α sets decoding quality**, and nothing else does: at equal α the shared basis and
  per-chunk U decode identically. The defaults are ε = 100 and α = 7; see the
  [table on the home page](../index.qmd#choosing-α) for α = 14 and 2.5.
- **More rank does not pay**: ε = 70 matches ε = 100 and ε = 50 is slightly worse per byte.
- **The spatial part is exhausted at m ≈ 24–32** vectors (1–4 % of the file); m = 16
  loses up to 1.6 dB.
- **Keep the coefficients in float16**: int8 saves 1–5 % of the bytes at unchanged SNR but
  degrades decoding on most recordings. SNR is a poor proxy for decoding.
